items.message:
Forecast high river levels overnight may lead to flooding.
Flooding is possible from overnight on Saturday 24 October into Sunday 25 October.
Flooding may affect low lying land and roads along the River Wye from Hay on Wye to Ross on Wye. Other locations affected may include the A438 between Letton & Willersey, Byford, Bredwardine & Hereford. Road closures & diversions on the A438 may be in force. Predicted peaks:- Hay on Wye 1.8m to 2.1m on 25/10 AM, Bredwardine 3.7m to 4.0m on 25/10 AM, Belmont 3.8 to 4.1m on 25/10 AM, Old Wye Bridge 3.3m to 3.6m on 25/10 AM, Mordiford 3.4m to 3.7m on 25/10 PM, and Ross on Wye 2.9m to 3.2m on 25/10 PM.
We are closely monitoring the situation .
Take care and avoid walking, cycling or driving through flood water.  
This message will be updated by 10:00AM on Sunday 25 October or as the situation changes.

High tides, strong winds and large waves today may lead to flooding. 
Flooding is possible during Saturday evening and Sunday morning. 
Areas most at risk include the Severn Estuary at Severn Beach including New Passage and Pilning.	
						
The detailed tidal forecast for those who use it is for a peak level at Avonmouth of 7.01 mAODN at 6:45 PM on Saturday 24/10/2026, which is 0.79 m above tide tables, with South Westerly force 7 winds. (mAODN is height above average sea level.)	
		
The second forecast high water is at 7:15 AM on Sunday 25/10/2026 with a level of 7.09 mAODN which is 0.78 m above tide tables, with Westerly force 7 winds. 
We are closely monitoring the situation and will issue further Alerts or updates as necessary. 
Avoid beaches and coastal promenades, which may be flooded. Tides remain high until Thursday though wind conditions will improve. 
This message will be updated by 12:00PM on Sunday 25 October or as the situation changes.
